quantifiers: there exist r fixed G-invariant eta_i
the unit-cell L1 error is strictly below epsilon

steps.statement: A unit cell modulo the translation lattice is a compact torus of finite positive measure.
The real trigonometric polynomial algebra contains constants, separates points, and is closed under conjugation; Stone-Weierstrass gives uniform density in continuous periodic functions.
For a G-invariant f, Reynolds averaging any uniform approximant q gives q_G in P_torus^G and ||f-q_G||_infinity <= ||f-q||_infinity.
P_torus^G is a free module of rank r=[Wa:G] over P_torus^Wa with fixed G-invariant module basis eta_1,...,eta_r.
The invariant polynomial q_G decomposes exactly as sum_i p_i eta_i with p_i in P_torus^Wa, hence continuous Wa-invariant h_i=p_i.
The unit-cell L1 error is at most |Omega| times the uniform error.
Choosing the pre-averaging uniform error below epsilon/(2|Omega|) yields strict L1 error below epsilon for every epsilon>0.

bound_certificate.note: Positive numerical representatives machine-check the symbolic inequality; the derivation uses symbols epsilon and |Omega|.

noncircularity: No target, sample, basis budget, tolerance, or fit result is selected from an observed error. The proof chooses a uniform approximation tolerance from epsilon and finite cell measure before constructing the approximant.
